narr: An elongated surface trough slowly moved through south Texas on June 3rd, with ample Gulf moisture in place across the Lower Rio Grande Valley. This allowed for thunderstorms to develop, leading to heavy rain falling across portions of the Lower Rio Grande Valley, focused on Starr and Hidalgo County near the river. Eventually, enough rain fell to cause flash flooding and street flooding across portions of each county.
ev: The Starr County Sheriff's Office reported that San Juan Drive in Garceno, west of Rio Grande City, was flooded with at least 2 feet of water, causing traffic to divert away from the area.

Report received from the public, via the MPing app but confirmed with social media reports, of streets flooded with some vehicles stranded as well along Griffin Parkway north of the center of Mission.
lsr: STARR COUNTY SHERIFFS OFFICE REPORTED THAT SAN JUAN STREET IN GARCENO WAS FLOODED AND TRAFFIC WAS DIVERTING.
